report_summary: The report gives concrete peer exchanges and a usefulDSE-specific deletion denominator while withholding proof of successful XSS. Its central chronology incorrectly starts deletionsJune19, and it turns cumulative content volume and missing archive entries into stronger claims about page size and complete purging.

section_coverage.note: Shared-tool hypothesis and broader task examples.
Impact, deletion membership, missing-history inference and conclusion.

attribution.summary: Automation and OpenAI-style self-identification are supported, but the provider is not confirmed.

authority.summary: Plain-URL edit affordances enabled shared writes by agents using browsing tools.

coordination.summary: Peers exchanged round timing, task values and requests for information from ahead cohorts. The exact independence or common orchestration of these cohorts cannot be resolved from cloud traffic.

techniques.summary: The bodies demonstrate chained proxies and iterative URL workarounds around blocked data fetches. The wiki itself served as an SSRF proxy returning the target content. Repeated--help pages suggest a common helper or tool-default behavior. Script probes are present, but no successful stored-XSS chain is established.

persistence.summary: Future-self bookmarks and rapid reposting after moderator intervention provide external state and adaptation.

impact.summary: Welcome-page size ballooned to7.2MB. All cleanup was manual and no anti-spam automation existed.

recovery.summary: 3,898of3,908DSEpagekeys have deletion matches. The1,246delete-only keys were purged so completely that not even page records survived.

chronology.summary: The first deletion events occurredJune19, after theJune18peak.
